indication: advanced wild-type (KIT/PDGFRA-WT) GIST; also PPGL, pNET, VHL-associated tumors, HIF-2α-altered solid tumors
biomarker: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type GIST (the dSDH cohort is the canonical wt-GIST subset)
inclusion_match_notes: The wt-GIST cohort accepts KIT/PDGFRA-WT advanced GIST, which is exactly this patient's molecular subtype. Two blockers right now: the patient is NED post-R0 so there is no RECIST-measurable disease to enroll on, and the SDH-deficient driver call still needs SDHA/SDHB IHC re-stain plus germline SDHA resolution before the sponsor will accept the dSDH-GIST label. Flag as a contingency option for first recurrence.
intervention_dosing: belzutifan 120 mg PO once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity

biomarker: SDH-mutant or SDH-deficient GIST (SDHA / SDHB / SDHC / SDHD mutation or SDHB-IHC loss)
intervention: temozolomide 85 mg/m^2 PO daily x 21 days every 28 days
inclusion_match_notes: SDH-deficient driver matches the trial's first inclusion criterion; the patient's biallelic SDHA call would qualify once tumor-tissue SDHA/SDHB IHC and germline SDHA confirm the phenotype. The trial is active-not-recruiting (last verified Aug 2024) and the readout has not yet been published, so even at recurrence this is a watch-for-data row rather than an enroll-now option. Asan's NCT05661643 is the parallel enrolling trial.
intervention_dosing: TMZ 85 mg/m^2 PO daily, days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle, minimum 6 months

biomarker: KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST with SDH deficiency (SDHB-IHC loss or SDHx mutation); exploratory cohort of WT-GIST without SDH deficiency
intervention: temozolomide 200 mg/m^2 PO daily x 5 days every 28 days
endpoint: objective response rate in the SDH-deficient WT-GIST cohort (RECIST 1.1)
inclusion_match_notes: The primary cohort requires KIT/PDGFRA-WT plus SDH deficiency, which the patient meets once SDHA/SDHB IHC and germline SDHA confirm the call. This is the enrolling temozolomide trial right now (last verified Apr 2026). Two practical issues: the trial is based in Korea (Asan Medical Center) so feasibility depends on travel, and measurable disease is required so the row is contingent on first recurrence.
intervention_dosing: TMZ 200 mg/m^2 PO daily, days 1-5 of a 28-day cycle

intervention: pemigatinib PO daily on days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle
inclusion_match_notes: Newest SDH-deficient-GIST trial (start Apr 2026) and an interesting mechanism bet — preclinical work shows FGFR1/3 and FGF3/4 upregulation in dSDH-GIST. The 24-patient design is small. Same gating as the other dSDH trials: measurable disease required, SDH-deficient phenotype must be pathologist-confirmed. Suzanne George at DFCI is the contact and would be the logical referral path.
intervention_dosing: pemigatinib PO daily, days 1-14 of a 21-day cycle

indication: wild-type GIST, SDH-deficient PPGL, HLRCC-associated RCC
biomarker: KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST or SDH-deficient PPGL or HLRCC-mutated RCC
design: open-label, single-arm phase 2 (terminated for low accrual)
intervention: guadecitabine (SGI-110) 45 mg/m^2 SC daily x 5 every 28 days
inclusion_match_notes: The mechanism story (DNA hypermethylation in dSDH-GIST -> hypomethylating agent) is exactly right for this patient, but the readout was negative — 0/9 responses across 7 wt-GIST, 1 PPGL, 1 HLRCC. The trial closed for low accrual before reaching its 70-patient target. Kept for the board's mechanism-context dossier: hypomethylating agents are off the table for this patient even at recurrence.
intervention_dosing: guadecitabine 45 mg/m^2 SC days 1-5 of a 28-day cycle

endpoint: RECIST 1.1 response rate at 6 months; clinical benefit rate at 9 months
effect_size: 0/20 ORR; 40% clinical benefit at 9 mo; mTTP 9.1 mo
inclusion_match_notes: Mechanism (IGF-1R / insulin-receptor inhibition) was anchored on early dSDH-GIST data showing IGF1R overexpression. Readout was a hard negative on ORR (0/20) with a 40% clinical-benefit rate that may reflect dSDH-GIST's natural indolence rather than drug activity. Kept as legacy-research context so the board sees the IGF1R hypothesis has been tested and is off the table.

indication: rare solid tumors (SDH-deficient GIST explicitly on the eligible list)
biomarker: SDH-deficient GIST or other rare-tumor / tumor-predisposition phenotype
design: longitudinal natural-history observational registry with biospecimen acquisition
intervention: no investigational drug; clinical evaluation, imaging, germline + tumor genomics
inclusion_match_notes: Open to SDH-deficient GIST patients regardless of disease status, so the NED-post-R0 setting is not a blocker. The right entry point into the NCI Pediatric and Wild-Type GIST referral network that the target_validation file called out for SDHC-methylation testing. Pairs naturally with the surveillance plan: registry enrollment, then specialist-clinic follow-up at NIH on top of community-based imaging.
aliases: NCI Rare Tumor Natural History Study
NCI Pediatric Oncology Branch rare-tumor protocol

indication: tumor-agnostic, off-label molecularly-matched basket — NF1 or MAP2K1 alteration cohort
biomarker: NF1 LOF or MAP2K1 activating mutation
intervention: cobimetinib 60 mg PO daily, days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle
inclusion_match_notes: MAP2K1 P124S is a known activating hotspot, so on paper the MEGALiT NF1/MAP2K1 arm matches. Two big caveats: the variant is currently ctDNA-only and tissue confirmation is gated by the FoundationOne CDx re-test from the validation plan, and the trial is active-not-recruiting (last update suggests the cohort is no longer enrolling). Kept as a potential MEK arm if tissue confirms the variant and another MEK basket opens at recurrence.
intervention_dosing: cobimetinib 60 mg PO daily, days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle

intervention: trametinib +/- vebreltinib (MET inhibitor) on MAP2K1-alteration arm
inclusion_match_notes: Active MAP2K1-alteration basket arm. Same blockers as MEGALiT — MAP2K1 P124S is ctDNA-only right now, tissue confirmation is essential, and the trial is run from a Chinese-academic consortium so feasibility depends on geography. Worth tracking at recurrence if the variant is confirmed clonal in tumor.
intervention_dosing: trametinib 2 mg PO daily (+/- vebreltinib per arm)

indication: PIK3CA-mutant advanced solid tumors and HR+/HER2- breast cancer
design: first-in-human dose-escalation + expansion, monotherapy and combination
inclusion_match_notes: PIK3CA-mutant solid-tumor basket open at multiple US sites. Real obstacle: R93W sits outside the validated alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots (E542K/E545K/H1047R/C420R) and the call is ctDNA-only, so this trial would need the FoundationOne CDx tissue confirmation plus a sponsor-by-sponsor variant-eligibility check before it could be considered. Lowest-confidence row in the dossier given the non-canonical variant.

indication: advanced/relapsed renal cancer and other HIF-stabilizing malignancies (SDHx-mutated PGL/PPGL expansion arm planned)
inclusion_match_notes: Trial terminated Feb 2026 for business reasons; the SDHx-mutation expansion arm 1B never opened. Kept in the dossier so the board sees the HIF-2α pipeline beyond belzutifan has been thinned out — next-gen HIF-2α (DFF332, NKT-2152) both discontinued in 2025-2026, leaving belzutifan as the sole active HIF-2α option.
intervention_dosing: DFF332 PO daily (dose-escalation; never reached expansion)

indication: metastatic SDH-deficient GIST and paraganglioma (case report)
inclusion_match_notes: Single-patient case of multiply-relapsed dSDH-GIST + PGL with clinical response to PARP + TMZ. Not a trial — kept because it's the only published evidence for the PARP-plus-alkylator strategy in this molecular subtype and the board will want to know it exists when discussing contingency options at recurrence.
intervention_dosing: olaparib 300 mg PO BID + temozolomide (dosing per case report)

indication: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type GIST molecular subtype landscape (review/registry analysis from the NIH Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic)
design: NIH Pediatric & Wild-Type GIST Clinic cohort analysis — molecular subtyping with treatment exposure data
endpoint: treatment exposure + response stratified by molecular subtype
effect_size: dSDH-GIST: response to imatinib rare; clinical benefit to sunitinib better than imatinib
inclusion_match_notes: Landmark Boikos/Helman 2016 paper from the NIH Pediatric & wt-GIST Clinic — defines the molecular subtype landscape this patient sits in and is the published reference for sunitinib as the preferred 2L TKI in dSDH-GIST (better than imatinib, which has near-zero response in this subset). Not a trial enrollment row; it's the evidence anchor that the board will cite when sequencing TKI options at first recurrence.
intervention_dosing: sunitinib 50 mg PO daily x 4 weeks every 6 weeks (label dose for 2L GIST)

effect_size: regorafenib activity in dSDH-GIST: modest, similar to KIT-mutant 3L setting
inclusion_match_notes: von Mehren 2025 review summarises the current dSDH-GIST systemic-therapy stack — sunitinib then regorafenib then ripretinib remains the TKI backbone, with belzutifan and temozolomide as the trial-territory targeted options. The row anchors the regorafenib evidence base for the contingency plan rather than pointing at a specific trial.
intervention_dosing: regorafenib 160 mg PO daily x 3 weeks every 4 weeks (label dose)

indication: rare GIST subtypes (SDH-deficient, NF1, BRAF-mutant) — review
effect_size: ripretinib activity in dSDH-GIST: case-level only, no prospective wt-GIST cohort data
inclusion_match_notes: Mavroeidis 2025 covers rare-GIST sequencing and notes that ripretinib has the weakest evidence base in dSDH-GIST of the three post-imatinib TKIs because INVICTUS enrolled vanishingly few wt-GIST patients. Kept as the 4L anchor for the contingency plan — likely to be tried after sunitinib and regorafenib have been exhausted.
